metaDescription: The best budget countertop dishwashers for 2026, with honest notes on capacity, faucet versus tank setups, noise and what small models cannot fit.
expertTake: The COMFEE 6 place model with eight programs is our top budget pick because it is a proven size with faucet hookup and an Energy Star listing. The Hamilton Beach is the value pick for a simple, familiar machine. Skip countertop dishwashers if you cook for four or more, because six place settings fill after one family dinner.
introParagraphs: A countertop dishwasher is a small machine that sits beside the sink and washes about six place settings. It suits apartments, dorms, RVs and renters who cannot install a built-in unit, and it uses less water than handwashing a full load.

The real decision is setup and capacity. Some need a faucet adaptor, others fill from a built-in tank, and none will hold large pots or sheet pans. Measure your counter and the tallest dish you own before you choose a model.

products.name: COMFEE Countertop Dishwasher 6 Place 8 Programs Energy Star

specList.label: Size
specList.value: 19.7 x 21.7 x 17.2 inches (D x W x H)

products.description:
The COMFEE is the most complete small machine in this lineup, with six place settings, eight wash programs including a speed cycle and an Energy Star listing. It connects directly to a kitchen faucet with a suitable adaptor, so it needs no plumbing work, though you must be near a tap and a drain.

Against the EUHOMY it is larger and needs a faucet, so it cannot sit in an RV without a hookup. Against the Hamilton Beach it gives more programs and a more modern feature set. It ranks first because the capacity, programs and efficiency listing combine into the best balance of a small machine.

The footprint is roughly 20 by 22 inches, so it takes a good share of counter space. Rinse off food scraps, load dishes with the dirtiest surfaces facing the spray, and run it when the tank or hose is connected. Clean the filter every week. Expect no room for large pots, sheet pans or tall pitchers, and plan on handwashing those.

products.badge: Best for No Hookup and Quiet
products.name: EUHOMY Portable Countertop Dishwasher 40 dB No Hookup

specList.label: Programs
specList.value: 6 including Normal, ECO, Quick, Baby Care

specList.label: Dry cycle
specList.value: Fresh mode lasting up to 73 hours

products.description:
The EUHOMY is the best pick if you cannot or will not connect to a faucet. You can pour water into its built-in 5 L tank or use a hose, so it works in an RV, a dorm or a rental with an awkward sink. Its 40 dB rating is quiet enough to run in an open plan flat.

Against the COMFEE it has fewer programs and a smaller practical load, but it is more flexible about where it sits. Against the delay-start model it lacks scheduling but is quieter. It ranks second because tank filling is a chore on every cycle, and a small tank limits how many dishes you can wash per fill.

Use softened or filtered water if your tap is hard, since mineral scale builds up on the heater and spray arms. Empty the drain hose to a sink or bucket after each run. Clean the filter weekly and wipe the door gasket. The fresh mode helps keep dishes from smelling musty if you cannot unload right away, which is useful in a busy household because a closed, damp tub is where stale smells start. Always leave the door cracked once the dishes are out.

products.name: Compact Countertop Dishwasher Delay Start 5+1 Programs 167°F

specList.label: Size

products.description:
The delay-start model is the narrowest machine here, just over 16 inches wide and 15.5 inches deep. That makes it the pick for a small kitchen or a shelf, and the delay start lets you run a cycle later, which is handy for night-time or off-peak use. A high heat setting up to 167 degrees F helps with greasy plates.

Compared with the COMFEE it offers fewer programs and a smaller internal space, so it handles fewer plates. Against the EUHOMY it adds a delay function but its noise is not stated as precisely. It ranks third because small interior space is the price of the small footprint, and its brand is less established.

Check how many of your own plates and bowls fit before you commit, since a narrow tub limits platter size, since a dinner plate over about 10 inches may not stand upright, and mugs and glasses need the top rack. If your everyday dishes are large, a wider machine is the safer choice. Scrape plates and place bowls at an angle for the dual spray. Clean the filter every week and wipe the door gasket. If you cook large meals often, expect to handwash big pots and pans separately.

products.name: COMFEE Portable Countertop Dishwasher 1.32 Gal Tank 6 Programs

specList.label: Programs

products.description:
This COMFEE variant uses a built-in 1.32 gallon tank, so it works without a faucet hookup. It has a Hygiene cycle that heats water up to 158 degrees F and an Air Refresh mode that circulates air to keep dishes from smelling stale. The program set also includes Fruit and Glass cycles.

Against the faucet-connected COMFEE it is easier to place anywhere, but it needs refilling each run. Against the EUHOMY it has a hotter hygiene cycle but a less certain noise level. It ranks fourth because a tank-only machine means the same tank limit as the EUHOMY, and the first-place COMFEE offers more programs.

Fill the tank with clean water to the line and do not overload the racks. The hot hygiene cycle suits baby bottles and cutting boards, though plastic items must be dishwasher safe. Clean the filter weekly and leave the door slightly open after a cycle so the interior can air out. Hard water will scale the heater over time.

products.name: Hamilton Beach HBDW3208 Countertop Dishwasher 6 Place
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach is a plain, familiar countertop dishwasher that holds six standard place settings and connects to a kitchen tap. It is the sort of machine that suits renters who want a known brand name and no extras. The description highlights low water use, which is the main reason to own one.

Against the COMFEE it offers fewer programs and a less modern feature set, but it is a simple machine with a known maker. Against the delay-start model it has more capacity but a wider body. It ranks last because the specifics are thinner and newer models add efficiency listings and hygiene cycles.

Check that your faucet accepts the included adaptor before you buy, since some pull-out or specialty taps do not. Pre-rinse heavily soiled dishes, because simple cycles are not built to scrub baked-on food. Clean the filter weekly and run a vinegar cycle monthly to prevent scale. Spare parts and support are easier to find for a mainstream brand, which counts for a machine with wear parts like a filter basket, a drain hose and a door seal, whereas a budget model from a small seller may leave you without a replacement after two years.
products.bestFor: Renters who want a plain machine from a known brand.

Six place settings suits two or three people

Simple controls with no learning curve

buyingCriteria.explanation: Six place settings is the standard size for a countertop model and suits two or three people. Four place machines hold much less. The common mistake is expecting pots, sheet pans and tall pitchers to fit. In this lineup the COMFEE 6 place and the Hamilton Beach hold six, while the narrow delay-start unit holds less.

Faucet models, like the COMFEE 6 place and Hamilton Beach, draw water from a tap with an adaptor and drain to the sink. Tank models, like the EUHOMY and the COMFEE 1.32 gallon, let you pour water in and work without plumbing. Tanks suit RVs and rentals but add a refill chore each cycle. Check your faucet thread before you buy. Many kitchen taps have an aerator that unscrews to reveal a standard thread, but pull-down and sensor faucets often have no thread at all. A quick look under the aerator, or a measurement of its diameter, saves a return.

These machines are bulky. The COMFEE is about 20 by 22 inches while the delay-start unit is just over 16 inches wide. Measure the counter, the height under the cabinet and the door swing. A taller front-loading door needs clearance to open.

Useful cycles include normal, eco, quick and a hot hygiene mode. The COMFEE tank model reaches 158 degrees F and the delay-start model reaches 167 degrees F. Higher heat helps with grease and baby items but is hard on some plastics. Eight programs are nice, but a good normal cycle matters most. Most owners settle on two cycles, a normal wash and a quick one, and ignore the rest. Pay for programs only if you will actually use the hygiene or glass settings.

Noise ranges from about 40 dB for the EUHOMY to over 50 dB for some others. In an open plan flat, a quiet machine matters. Most countertop units are louder than a built-in because they have less insulation. Check the listed decibel number. A lab figure is taken on a quiet surface, so a machine sitting on a hollow counter or touching a cabinet can sound louder. A thin rubber mat under the feet takes the edge off the hum and the rattle.

A small dishwasher uses a few liters per cycle, less than handwashing a full load. The COMFEE 6 place lists an Energy Star rating. Short eco cycles save more but take longer. Hard water reduces efficiency by scaling the heater, so a softener or filter helps. Rinse aid and a periodic vinegar run keep the interior clear, and a half-empty load wastes the same water as a full one, so wait until the racks are mostly stocked.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared place settings and dimensions against realistic dish loads. The COMFEE 6 place is about 20 inches deep while the delay-start unit is 15.5 inches. We favoured sizes that match small households.

howWeEvaluated.title: Setup and hookup
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at faucet versus tank filling, adaptor needs and drain arrangements. Tank models suit RVs, while faucet models need a nearby tap. Ease of setup counted heavily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Programs and heat
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the program lists and top temperatures. The COMFEE offers eight programs and the delay-start unit reaches 167°F. Owner feedback patterns show quick and normal cycles are used most.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and daily use
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked decibel claims and control layouts. The EUHOMY rates 40 dB. We rewarded quiet running and simple controls in a small home.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value versus compromise
howWeEvaluated.description: Each pick sits in the lower half of the price range. We weighed what each gives up, such as capacity, programs or hookup, and whether a handwashing habit would still be needed.

cards.label: COMFEE 6 place (faucet)
cards.text: No refilling, a full load of water each cycle and an Energy Star listing. It needs a compatible tap.

cards.label: EUHOMY (tank)
cards.text: Works anywhere with an outlet and a drain. You refill the tank each cycle and the load is limited.

howToChoose.note: Pick the faucet model if you have a normal tap. Pick the tank model for RVs, dorms and awkward sinks.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A quiet rating, a footprint that fits your counter and a setup you can reverse when you move. Check your landlord's rules on faucet adaptors.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EUHOMY is the quietest and needs no plumbing. The delay-start unit is the narrowest and can run at off-peak times.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cook for four or more, need space for pots and pans, or want a built-in dishwasher with much stronger cleaning. A full-size machine handles more and runs quieter.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cook for one to three people and handwash pots anyway. A budget countertop model cuts daily dish time.

maintenance.why: Food scraps clog the filter and reduce spray pressure. Rinse it under the tap and refit it firmly.
Residue builds up on the seal and causes odours. A damp cloth keeps it clean.
Hard water leaves scale on the heater and spray arm. A vinegar or descaler run restores performance.
Mineral deposits block spray holes and leave dishes dirty. A toothpick clears them.
Leaks usually start at the faucet adaptor or drain hose. Replace worn washers before they fail.

faq.a: Faucet models need a tap adaptor and a drain hose, but no permanent plumbing. Tank models need only an outlet and a place to drain. Both can be removed when you move.

faq.q: Is a countertop dishwasher worth it for one or two people?
faq.a: Yes, if you hate handwashing and have the counter space. It saves daily dish time, though pots and pans usually still need handwashing. Six place settings fills quickly.

faq.q: How clean do the dishes get?
faq.a: They clean well if you scrape plates and load properly. Heavily baked-on food needs pre-rinsing. Small machines move less water than full-size units, so scrape plates and rinse off sauces that dry hard, such as egg or oatmeal. Hard water can leave spots without rinse aid.
Many owners do, especially with quiet models such as the EUHOMY. Check the hoses, keep the drain clear and never leave it unattended with a loose hose.

faq.q: Do these use less water than handwashing?
faq.a: Usually, if you wash a full load. Small tanks use only a few liters per cycle. Running half loads erases the saving.
Most are louder than a built-in. The EUHOMY rates 40 dB, but real use can be louder. Place it on a stable, vibration-free surface to reduce noise.
